title: Economy & Business
description: Discuss money, banking, commerce, and basic economics. Learn vocabulary for financial transactions, business entities, and economic concepts. Practice the present tense for routines, the past tense for purchases, formal commands for business interactions, and conditional for hypothetical financial situations.

grammar.title: Present Tense for Financial Routines
grammar.content:
The present tense is used to describe daily financial and commercial routines — going to the bank, making purchases, and talking about business habits.

Regular conjugations:

-AR verbs (pagar, ahorrar, cobrar):
  yo pago / tú pagas / usted paga / nosotros pagamos / vosotros pagáis / ellos pagan
  yo ahorro / tú ahorras / usted ahorra / nosotros ahorramos / vosotros ahorráis / ellos ahorran

-ER verbs (comprar, gastar, ganar):
  yo compro / tú compras / usted compra / nosotros compramos / vosotros compráis / ellos compran
  yo gasto / tú gastas / usted gasta / nosotros gastamos / vosotros gastáis / ellos gastan

-IR verbs (cobrar, vender, servir):
  yo cobro / tú cobras / usted cobra / nosotros cobramos / vosotros cobráis / ellos cobran

Common business expressions in the present:

1. I go to the bank every Monday:
   Voy al banco todos los lunes.

2. I pay by credit card:
   Pago con tarjeta de crédito.

3. This costs 20 euros:
   Esto cuesta 20 euros.

4. I save money every month:
   Ahorro dinero todos los meses.

5. The shop is open from 9 to 6:
   La tienda está abierta de nueve a seis.

Irregular present tense you need:
  ir → voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van (to go to the bank)
  tener → tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen (to have an account)
  poner → pongo, pones, pone, ponemos, ponéis, ponen (to put money in)
  salir → salgo, sales, sale, salimos, salís, salen (to leave the store)
  hacer → hago, haces, hace, hacemos, hacéis, hacen (to do business)
  decir → digo, dices, dice, decimos, decís, dicen (to say the price)
  venir → vengo, vienes, viene, venimos, venís, vienen (to come to the store)
  conocer → conozco, conoces, conoce, conocemos, conocéis, conocen (to know the price)
examples: Voy al banco todos los lunes para retirar dinero. (I go to the bank every Monday to withdraw money.)
Pago con tarjeta porque es más seguro. (I pay by card because it's safer.)
¿Cuánto cuesta este producto? (How much does this product cost?)
Ahorro dinero cada mes para las vacaciones. (I save money every month for vacations.)
La empresa tiene 50 empleados. (The company has 50 employees.)
Mi jefe trabaja en la oficina central. (My boss works at the main office.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian present tense is very similar to Spanish — both use the infinitive stem + personal endings. Romanian: 'eu merg la bancă' = Spanish 'voy al banco', 'eu plătesc cu cardul' = Spanish 'pago con tarjeta'. The key difference is Spanish has many more irregular verbs in the present (ir, tener, hacer, decir, venir, poner, conocer), which don't exist in Romanian. For Romanian speakers, the regular verb patterns are nearly identical — just memorize the irregular forms.

grammar.title: Pretérito Indefinido for Past Purchases and Transactions
grammar.content:
The preterite tense is used to describe specific past purchases, banking transactions, and business events.

Regular conjugations:

-AR verbs (pagar, comprar, trabajar):
  yo pagué / tú pagaste / usted pagó / nosotros pagamos / vosotros pagasteis / ellos pagaron
  yo compré / tú compraste / usted compró / nosotros compramos / vosotros comprasteis / ellos compraron

-ER/-IR verbs (vender, cobrar, servir):
  yo vendí / tú vendiste / usted vendió / nosotros vendimos / vosotros vendisteis / ellos vendieron
  yo cobré / tú cobraste / usted cobró / nosotros cobramos / vosotros cobrasteis / ellos cobraron

Important note: -AR verb endings in preterite use -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron (accent on first and third person). -ER/-IR verbs use -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron (accent on first person singular).

Common past business expressions:

1. I bought a new phone last week:
   Compré un teléfono nuevo la semana pasada.

2. I paid with cash at the store:
   Pagué en efectivo en la tienda.

3. The company sold 100 units:
   La empresa vendió 100 unidades.

4. I withdrew 500 euros from the ATM:
   Retiré 500 euros del cajero automático.

5. We earned a good salary this year:
   Ganamos un buen salario este año.

Irregular preterite verbs:
  ser/ir → fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron (I went / I was)
  tener → tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos, tuvisteis, tuvieron (I had)
  hacer → hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron (I did)
  decir → dije, dijiste, dijo, dijimos, dijisteis, dijeron (I said)
  poner → puse, pusiste, puso, pusimos, pusisteis, pusieron (I put)
  venir → vine, viniste, vino, vinimos, vinisteis, vinieron (I came)
  saber → supe, supiste, supo, supimos, supisteis, supieron (I found out)
  poder → pude, pudiste, pudo, pudimos, pudisteis, pudieron (I could)
examples: Ayer compré unos zapatos en la tienda. (Yesterday I bought some shoes at the store.)
Pagué con tarjeta de débito. (I paid with a debit card.)
La empresa vendió todos sus productos. (The company sold all its products.)
Mi jefe me dio un aumento de sueldo. (My boss gave me a salary increase.)
Fuimos al banco a abrir una cuenta. (We went to the bank to open an account.)
Hicimos una inversión importante este año. (We made an important investment this year.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian perfective past (perfectul simplu / mai mult ca perfectul) corresponds roughly to Spanish preterite. Romanian: 'am cumpărat' = Spanish 'compré', 'am plătit' = Spanish 'pagué'. The key difference: Spanish preterite has distinct forms for all persons, while Romanian often uses the compound 'am + past participle' form. For Romanian speakers, the Spanish preterite endings are new but follow a regular pattern. The irregular forms (fui, tuve, hice, etc.) must be memorized — there's no Romanian equivalent.

grammar.title: Formal Commands (Usted/Ustedes) for Business Interactions
grammar.content:
Formal commands are essential in business situations — when speaking to customers, clients, suppliers, and colleagues.

Formation — AFIRMATIVO:
- -AR verbs: yo form minus -o + -e (sg) / -en (pl)
  pagar → pague / paguen (pay)
  cobrar → cobre / cobren (charge)
  trabajar → trabaje / trabajen (work)
- -ER/-IR verbs: yo form minus -o + -a (sg) / -an (pl)
  comprar → compre / compren (buy)
  vender → venda / vendan (sell)
  servir → sirva / sirvan (serve)

Formation — NEGATIVO:
- -AR verbs: no + present subjunctive (-e / -en)
- -ER/-IR verbs: no + present subjunctive (-a / -an)

Essential business commands:

Afirmativo:
  - Abra la cuenta, por favor. (Open the account, please.)
  - Cierre la cuenta mañana. (Close the account tomorrow.)
  - Déme la factura, por favor. (Give me the receipt, please.)
  - Espere un momento. (Wait a moment.)
  - Venga a nuestra oficina. (Come to our office.)
  - Tome asiento. (Have a seat.)
  - Diga el nombre completo. (Say your full name.)
  - Salga por la puerta de la derecha. (Exit through the right door.)

Negativo:
  - No espere aquí. (Don't wait here.)
  - No firmen hasta que les expliquemos. (Don't sign until we explain.)
  - No paguen todavía. (Don't pay yet.)
  - No vendan sin autorización. (Don't sell without authorization.)

Irregular formal commands:
  estar → esté / estén
  tener → tenga / tengan
  poner → ponga / pongan
  salir → salga / salgan
  hacer → haga / hagan
  venir → venga / vengan
  decir → diga / digan
  ir → vaya / vayan
  saber → sepa / sepan
  poder → pueda / puedan
  ser → sea / sean
examples: Abra la cuenta en la oficina de al lado. (Open the account at the office next door.)
Pague al cajero automático. (Pay at the ATM.)
No firmen el contrato sin leerlo. (Don't sign the contract without reading it.)
Déme su identificación, por favor. (Give me your identification, please.)
Venga a verme mañana. (Come see me tomorrow.)
Tenga paciencia, el proceso es rápido. (Have patience, the process is quick.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian formal commands use 'să + conjugated verb': 'să deschideți' = 'abra', 'să semnați' = 'firme', 'să așteptați' = 'espere'. This is nearly identical to the Spanish usted command structure. The Spanish subjunctive-based commands and Romanian 'să' commands function the same way — both are used for formal requests and instructions. For Romanian speakers: 'să plătiți' = 'paguen', 'să cumpărați' = 'compren', 'să vinți' = 'vengan'. The main difference is Spanish has more irregular forms that must be memorized.

grammar.title: Conditional and 'Si' Clauses for Financial Hypotheticals
grammar.content:
The conditional tense and 'si' clauses are used to discuss hypothetical financial situations — what you would buy, invest in, or do with money.

Conditional formation:
- Take the full infinitive + endings: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían
  pagar → pagaría, pagarías, pagaría, pagaríamos, pagaríais, pagarían
  comprar → compraría, comprarías, compraría, compraríamos, compraríais, comprarían
  ahorrar → ahorraría, ahorrarías, ahorraría, ahorraríamos, ahorraríais, ahorrarían

Irregular conditional stems:
  tener → tendría, tendrías, tendría... (I would have)
  poder → podría, podrías, podría... (I could)
  deber → debería, deberías, debería... (I should)
  salir → saldría, saldrías, saldría... (I would leave)
  hacer → haría, harías, haría... (I would do)
  poner → pondría, pondrías, pondría... (I would put)
  decir → diría, dirías, diría... (I would say)
  querer → querría, querrías, querría... (I would want)
  saber → sabría, sabrías, sabría... (I would know)
  venir → vendría, vendrías, vendría... (I would come)
  valer → valdría, valdrías, valdría... (I would be worth)

'SI' CLAUSES (real conditions):
- SI + present indicative → future or imperative
  Si tengo dinero, compraré un coche. (If I have money, I'll buy a car.)
  Si pagas con tarjeta, recibes un descuento. (If you pay with card, you get a discount.)

'SI' CLAUSES (unlikely conditions):
- SI + imperfect subjunctive → conditional
  Si tuviera más dinero, invertiría en la bolsa. (If I had more money, I'd invest in the stock market.)
  Si pudiera ahorrar más, viajaría al extranjero. (If I could save more, I'd travel abroad.)

Business conditional phrases:
  - Yo compraría... (I would buy...)
  - Yo invertiría... (I would invest...)
  - Sería más barato si... (It would be cheaper if...)
  - Tendría más beneficios si... (I would have more profit if...)
  - Podría ahorrar dinero si... (I could save money if...)
examples: Si tuviera más dinero, compraría una casa. (If I had more money, I'd buy a house.)
Si ahorra ahora, podrá viajar el próximo año. (If you save now, you'll be able to travel next year.)
Invertiría en la bolsa si tuviera el capital. (I'd invest in the stock market if I had the capital.)
Sería más barato si pagara en efectivo. (It would be cheaper if you paid in cash.)
¿Podría abrir una cuenta de ahorro? (Could you open a savings account?)
Nosotros invertiríamos en un negocio local. (We would invest in a local business.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian conditional uses 'aș + infinitive': 'aș cumpăra' = 'compraría', 'aș investi' = 'invertiría', 'aș economisi' = 'ahorraría'. The structure is very similar to Spanish conditional. Romanian 'dacă' (if) clauses work the same way as Spanish 'si' clauses: 'Dacă aș avea mai mulți bani, aș cumpăra o casă' = 'Si tuviera más dinero, compraría una casă.' The conditional tense formation and si-clause patterns are nearly identical in structure between Romanian and Spanish.

pronunciation.title: Economy & Business Pronunciation — Financial and Commercial Vocabulary
pronunciation.content:
Clear pronunciation of financial and business terms is crucial for everyday transactions and professional interactions.

Key pronunciation patterns:

1. Trailing '-ción' and '-sión' (stress on the 's' sound):
   - la economía = eh-koh-NOH-mee-ah
   - la inversión = in-veh-RSEE-ohn
   - la transacción = trahn-SAK-see-ohn
   - la condición = kon-Dee-see-OHN
   Note: '-ción' and '-sión' are always stressed on the 's'

2. The 'll' (y sound in most regions):
   - el billón = BYE-ee-ohn (y sound, not ll like 'billy')
   - la billetera = bye-ee-TEH-rah

3. The 'j' and 'g' before 'e/i' (soft g, like harsh 'h'):
   - el jefe = HEH-feh (j = harsh h)
   - la empresa = em-PREH-sah (no j/g, but good practice)
   - el gerente = heh-REN-teh (g before e = harsh h)
   - el servicio = seh-VEE-see-oh (v/c sound, not 'vee')

4. Rolled 'r' at the beginning of words and double 'rr':
   - el dinero = dee-NEH-roh (rolled r at end)
   - el banco = BAN-ko (no r)
   - el comercio = koh-MER-see-oh (rolled r)
   - la empresa = em-PREH-sah (rolled r)

5. Stress on '-ia' endings:
   - la economía = eh-koh-NOH-mee-ah
   - la compañía = koh-mpee-NYAH
   - la industria = in-DUS-trieh-ah

6. Silent 'h':
   - el dinero = dee-NEH-roh
   - el horario = oh-RAH-ree-oh
   - la empresa = em-PREH-sah
   - el producto = proh-DOHK-toh
   - la factura = fak-TOH-rah

7. The 'qu' before 'e/i' (hard k sound):
   - la quiebra = KYEH-brah
   - el presupuesto = preh-soo-PUEST-toh
   - la cuota = KWOH-tah

8. Diphthongs:
   - el dinero = dee-NEH-roh (ie = diphthong)
   - el precio = PREH-see-oh (ie = diphthong)
   - la oferta = oh-FER-tah (no diphthong)

9. The 'z' (s sound in Latin America, th sound in Spain):
   - el dinero = dee-NEH-roh (no z, but common pattern)
   - la oferta = oh-FER-tah
   - el sueldo = SOO-el-doh

10. The 'ñ' (ny sound):
   - la nación = nah-see-OHN
   - la compañía = koh-mpee-NYAH
   - el año = AH-nyoh

11. The 'b' and 'v' (nearly identical in Spanish):
   - la venta = BEN-tah
   - el valor = bahl-OR
   - vender = ben-DEHR

Practice pairs:
   barato = bah-RAH-toh (cheap) vs. caro = KAH-roh (expensive)
   cobrar = koh-BRAHR (to charge) vs. ahorrar = ah-oh-RAHR (to save)
   dinero = dee-NEH-roh (money) vs. ahorro = ah-OR-roh (savings)
examples: economía = eh-koh-NOH-mee-ah (stress on 'NOH', ía diphthong)
inversión = in-veh-RSEE-ohn (stress on 'SSEE', trailing -sión)
cajero automático = kah-HEH-roh ow-toh-MAH-tee-koh (rolled r, silent h)
tarjeta = tar-HEH-tah (j = harsh h, stress on 'HEH')
negocio = neh-GOH-see-oh (c before i = soft th/s in Spain, s in LatAm)
vendedor = beh-neh-DAHR (rolled r, stress on 'DAH')
salario = sah-LAH-ree-oh (stress on 'LAH')
factura = fak-TOH-rah (silent h, stress on 'TOH')
oferta = oh-FER-tah (stress on 'FER')
descuento = dehs-KWEHN-toh (scu = hard k sound, stress on 'KWEHN')

exercises.question: What is the Spanish word for 'money'?
exercises.explanation: 'El dinero' means 'money.' 'La moneda' = coin/currency, 'el billete' = banknote, 'la tarjeta' = card.

exercises.question: How do you say 'to pay' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Pagar' means 'to pay.' 'Recibir' = to receive, 'gastar' = to spend, 'ahorrar' = to save.

exercises.question: Complete with the present tense: 'Yo ____ (ahorrar) dinero cada mes.' (I save money every month.)
exercises.explanation: 'Ahorro' is the yo form of ahorrar (1st person singular present). 'Yo ahorro dinero cada mes' = I save money every month.

exercises.question: What does 'caro' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Caro' means 'expensive.' The opposite is 'barato' (cheap). 'Económico' means 'affordable' or 'economical.'

exercises.question: Complete with the preterite: 'Ayer yo ____ (comprar) un regalo.' (Yesterday I bought a gift.)
exercises.explanation: 'Compré' is the yo form of comprar in the preterite. -AR verbs in yo preterite end in -é: comprar → compré.

exercises.question: What is the Spanish word for 'bank'?
exercises.explanation: 'El banco' means 'bank.' 'La oficina' = office, 'el cajero' = ATM/clerk, 'la cuenta' = account.

exercises.question: What is the formal command (usted) of 'abrir' (to open)?
exercises.explanation: 'Abra' is the usted command of abrir. For -IR verbs: yo form abro → drop -o → abr + a = abra.

exercises.question: Complete with the conditional: 'Si tuviera más dinero, ____ (comprar) una casa.' (If I had more money, I would buy a house.)
exercises.explanation: 'Compraría' is the yo form of comprar in the conditional. Full infinitive + conditional ending: comprar + ía = compraría.

exercises.question: What does 'el cajero automático' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'El cajero automático' means 'the ATM' (automatic teller machine). 'Cajero' alone can mean 'teller' or 'clerk.'

exercises.question: Complete with the correct preterite of 'vender': 'La tienda ____ (vender) todos los productos.' (The shop sold all the products.)
exercises.explanation: 'Vendió' is the usted/él/ella form of vender in the preterite. -IR verbs in 3rd person preterite end in -ió: vender → vendió.

exercises.question: What does 'la deuda' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'La deuda' means 'the debt.' 'El depósito' = deposit, 'el recibo' = receipt, 'los ingresos' = income.

exercises.question: Complete with the formal command: '____ (pagar) con tarjeta, por favor.' (Pay with card, please.)
exercises.explanation: 'Pague' is the usted command of pagar. For -AR verbs: yo form pago → drop -o → pag + e = pague.

exercises.question: What does 'el beneficio' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'El beneficio' means 'profit' in a business context. The opposite is 'la pérdida' (loss).

exercises.question: Complete with the correct form of 'costar': '¿Cuánto ____ (costar) este producto?' (How much does this product cost?)
exercises.explanation: 'Cuesta' is the 3rd person singular of costar (e→ie stem-changing verb). '¿Cuánto cuesta?' = How much does it cost?

exercises.question: What is the opposite of 'caro' (expensive)?
exercises.explanation: 'Barato' means 'cheap,' the direct opposite of 'caro' (expensive). 'Económico' = affordable, 'gratis' = free.

exercises.question: Complete with the conditional: 'Nosotros ____ (invertir) en un negocio local si tuviéramos el dinero.' (We would invest in a local business if we had the money.)
exercises.explanation: 'Invertiríamos' is the nosotros form of invertir in the conditional. Full infinitive + ending: invertir + íamos = invertiríamos.

exercises.question: What does 'la factura' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'La factura' means 'invoice' or 'bill.' 'El recibo' is the smaller receipt you get after paying.

exercises.question: Complete with the preterite: 'Mi jefe me ____ (dar) un aumento de sueldo.' (My boss gave me a salary increase.)
exercises.explanation: 'Dio' is the 3rd person singular of dar in the preterite. Dar is irregular: di, diste, dio, dimos, disteis, dieron.

exercises.question: What does 'pagar en efectivo' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Pagar en efectivo' means 'to pay in cash.' 'Efectivo' = cash. The other options are: con tarjeta (card), con cheque (check), en cuotas (installments).

exercises.question: Complete with the formal negative command: 'No ____ (comprar) sin la factura.' (Don't buy without the receipt.)
exercises.explanation: 'Compre' is the negative usted command of comprar. For -ER verbs: no + present subjunctive (compra → compre). 'No compre sin la factura' = Don't buy without the receipt.
